title: Multicasting: Hot vs Cold, share, and shareReplay

questions.prompt: What distinguishes a hot (multicast) Observable from a cold (unicast) one?

options.text: A hot Observable shares one execution among all subscribers; a cold one runs the producer per subscriber
A hot Observable emits synchronously; a cold one emits asynchronously
A hot Observable can never complete
A cold Observable cannot be subscribed to more than once

questions.explanation: Multicasting shares a single source execution across subscribers (hot). Cold Observables create an independent producer for each subscription.

questions.prompt: Does a plain `share()` replay earlier values to a subscriber that joins later?

options.text: No — share() uses a Subject with no memory; late subscribers only see future values
Yes — it always replays the entire history
Yes — it replays exactly the last value
Only if the source is infinite

questions.explanation: share() multicasts through a plain Subject, so there is no replay. To give late subscribers past values, use shareReplay(n).

options.text: shareReplay(1) defaults to refCount:false, so it keeps the interval subscribed even after all subscribers leave
shareReplay always creates a new interval per subscriber
interval is not allowed inside shareReplay
shareReplay buffers every value forever

questions.explanation: With refCount:false (the default), shareReplay stays subscribed to the source after subscribers unsubscribe. Since interval never completes, it runs forever — a leak. Use { bufferSize: 1, refCount: true }.

questions.prompt: In `source$.pipe(expensive(), shareReplay(1), map(x => x))`, which operator runs per subscriber?

options.text: map — operators below shareReplay run per subscriber
expensive — operators above shareReplay run per subscriber
Both expensive and map run per subscriber
Neither — everything runs once

questions.explanation: Everything above the multicast operator is shared (runs once); everything below it runs independently for each subscriber. So expensive() is shared and map runs per subscriber.

questions.prompt: Make an infinite source multicast safely: `shareReplay({ bufferSize: 1, refCount: ______ })`. Type the boolean value.
questions.explanation: refCount: true unsubscribes from the source when the subscriber count drops to zero, so an infinite source stops when nobody is listening.

questions.prompt: Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: shareReplay(1) is fine for a completing HTTP source
multicast, publish, and refCount are deprecated in RxJS 7
share() is reference-counted by default
share() replays the last value to late subscribers

questions.explanation: shareReplay(1) safely caches completing sources; the publish/multicast/refCount family is deprecated in favor of share/shareReplay; share() is refCounted by default and has NO replay.
